# Environment-specific system arrangements

Manifold defines the core connection: needs are represented through requirements, and systems are intended to meet requirements. A system's usefulness is understood through its contribution to the relevant needs and requirements.

Whether systems work together, provide alternatives, share responsibilities or use another arrangement is determined by the particular requirements, needs, use cases and environment. A universal classification or combination rule for those arrangements is not a prerequisite for defining Manifold. Describing an arrangement in a particular case does not make that arrangement a rule of the standard.

Retain the accepted distinctions between intended and achieved contribution, partial and full fulfillment, and unknown and established results. A system's failure to satisfy every requirement does not erase a relevant partial contribution; an unknown contribution is not established absence of contribution. Existing requirement-origin and needs-adequacy provisions retain their scope.
